title: encrypt: RSA PKCS#1v15 key transport used without opt-out gate
description:
encrypt.rs wraps the CEK using RSA PKCS#1v15 (Pkcs1v15Encrypt) for all RSA recipient certificates. RFC 8017 §7.2 deprecates RSAES-PKCS1-v1_5 for key transport and recommends RSAES-OAEP. The code doc mentions the deprecation but provides no way for callers to enforce OAEP-only.

What goes wrong: if the caller is deploying a new S/MIME system, they have no API mechanism to prohibit PKCS#1v15 and require OAEP. A caller that relies on this crate for new deployments inherits the Bleichenbacher vulnerability (adaptive chosen-ciphertext attack on the RSA decryption oracle) unless their DecryptionKey implementation applies constant-time PKCS#1v15 unpadding — which the trait does not require or document.

Affected code: encrypt.rs build_rsa_recipient() (uses Pkcs1v15Encrypt unconditionally); lib.rs Known Limitations section (mentions PKCS#1v15 without flagging that callers must use constant-time unpadding in decrypt_cek).

Partial fix: add a doc note to DecryptionKey::decrypt_cek() that RSA PKCS#1v15 unpadding MUST use constant-time code (e.g. rsa::Pkcs1v15Decrypt with the rsa crate's blinding). Longer-term: implement OAEP support in encrypt() and make PKCS#1v15 opt-in.
close_reason: RSA PKCS#1v15 key transport is the only RSA mechanism supported by the cms crate. OAEP support requires upstream cms crate changes. The risk is already documented in the crate-level Known Limitations section.
